reviews.text:
I've been taking my guinea pigs here for checkups.

Three years ago, my guinea pig fractured its spine, but now it's incredibly healthy and thriving.

Currently, I'm taking another guinea pig here who has kidney stones.

All the veterinarians are kind and explain things thoroughly, which puts me at ease.

Thank you for your continued support.

A male doctor made a prescription error.

I gave my child the prescribed medication for two weeks and then returned to the clinic.

Doctor: "This medication contains XX..."
Me: "It doesn't contain XX."
Doctor: "It does!... (checks medical record) Oh, it doesn't."

It seems the crucial ingredient that affects the illness was missing. There was no acknowledgment of the mistake, nor any apology.

My child is left with lasting after-effects and now requires diapers and care.

I regret that if we hadn't come to this clinic, my child and I might not have had to suffer.

Even with an appointment, there is a waiting time, but the veterinarians and staff are very kind and explain the patient's condition in detail. The consultation fees are high, but pet owners can feel very at ease.

This is a long post.
Several of my birds have recently been treated here, and my 11-year-old Java sparrow has been on medication for sinusitis for about a month. The symptoms have spread to its beak during treatment, so the doctor said the condition was severe. However, it actually worsened during treatment and medication, and there was no improvement.
To summarize the treatment here and the doctor's opinion, first, the beak was deformed due to the sinusitis, so they advised against the beak trimming I requested.
Today, the avian specialist's opinion was that there was a curled deformity of the lower beak (caused by the worsening of the sinusitis) that had been overlooked there. The mouth was narrowed, making it difficult to eat properly, resulting in weight loss. They trimmed it immediately. There, they said that trimming the beak improperly could cause the bird to stop eating, so it's better not to trim it.
When I asked if they could perform nasal irrigation, they said it was not recommended because the pressure is quite strong.
Today, the avian specialist said that nasal irrigation was essential because pus had hardened firmly inside the nasal cavity, so they performed it. After the procedure, the nose cleared up a little and the cyanosis improved.
At your clinic, they said that when water was dripped into the nostrils, the bird opened and closed its beak, so it wasn't blocked.
In fact, the results from today's avian specialist showed that it was completely blocked, and although it wasn't breathing with its mouth open, it was breathing hard through the gap in its beak, indicating low oxygen levels and cyanosis on its beak.
The female veterinarian who substituted when the regular vet was unavailable said that cyanosis could also be a sign of decreased cardiac function. However, after today's nasal irrigation, the redness on the cyanotic beak quickly returned.

The avian specialist clearly explained that if the condition was worsening and the medication wasn't working, a diagnosis might be impossible, and then suggested a drug sensitivity test. This test would allow them to determine which medication was effective. According to that doctor, diagnosis can be impossible after a certain amount of antibiotic treatment. While that information is correct, I wish they had suggested the sensitivity test when I went for multiple checkups and the medication didn't seem to be working. A month of ineffective medication and four pointless nebulizer treatments without nasal irrigation were a waste of money. Today, I switched hospitals, and after nasal irrigation and injections, my bird's sleep time has decreased dramatically.
My only regret is not going to an avian specialist hospital from the beginning, but that hospital specializes in exotic animals and even has birds on its sign. They had various treatments, and some of the things I suggested were things I should have done, which is what I should have done at the avian specialist hospital today. Instead of saying "it's better not to do it," if you lack confidence in performing the procedure or the skill to do it on a small bird, shouldn't you clearly state that you cannot perform the procedure at your hospital, rather than saying "it's better not to do it"?
You completely failed to perform the necessary procedures.
You performed nebulizer treatment four times without any treatment, which had absolutely no effect. Apparently, nebulizing is ineffective because the mist doesn't reach the nasal cavity when the nose is blocked with pus. A bird specialist hospital only uses nebulizer treatment once the symptoms have improved. What was the point of your previous treatment? It's terrifying to think what would have happened if I had continued going there.

Before coming here, the symptoms were in one nostril and eye, but after starting treatment, instead of improving, they spread to both sides. I want a refund for the treatment costs (though that's impossible). From now on, I will go to a bird specialist hospital. While you treat exotic animals, I think you should remove birds from your list of services. The treatment process was very disappointing and sad.
I don't even want to give it one star; it's a negative rating.
The nearby hospital couldn't treat them, so we were referred here. The doctor is trustworthy and explained everything very carefully, and our puppies are doing well!

Thank you for your help.
My African fat-tailed gecko recently became ill, and I couldn't get an appointment at my usual clinic, so I visited your clinic for the first time.
The facility was clean, the reception staff were cheerful and kind, and the doctor who treated my gecko was very caring.
My gecko was diagnosed with rickets, and I gave him the prescribed medication and nutritional supplements.
He seemed a little better, but his symptoms didn't improve, and he passed away a few days later.
The doctor recommended hospitalization before he passed away, but I declined because I somehow wanted to let him stay at home.
Looking back, I wonder if something would have been different if I had hospitalized him, but I am very grateful for all the medication and injections you did.
The doctor was very gentle and careful in handling animals, and I felt at ease leaving my gecko in your care.
There are few hospitals that treat reptiles, so I would like to use your services again if anything happens to my gecko in the future.
Ideally, I should thank you in person, but I thought you might be busy, so I posted this here.

I took my rabbit to the vet.

It received an IV drip and an injection, but its symptoms did not improve at all.

Furthermore, the cost of the IV drip and injection alone was about 12,000 yen, which felt expensive. There was also no explanation or description of the ingredients in the prescribed medication, which left me feeling uneasy.

Afterward, I took it to another hospital, where it was determined that immediate hospitalization was necessary. The hospitalization cost about 20,000 yen for two days.

It has now recovered and is healthy, but I was disappointed with the treatment I received.

I received excellent care for my budgie.

The doctor was very kind and attentive during the examination.

After several visits, my budgie is now healthy and well.
I received help with my leopard gecko's egg-binding. It's only been a week since the surgery, but she's doing incredibly well. I'm filled with gratitude. Thank you so much.

"She called me crying!

Hahaha"

I don't know if they were talking about a customer, but I was bothered by the loud conversation of a young female staff member I overheard in the background during a phone reservation.

It was unpleasant to hear such a casual, school-break-like tone in a place where we deal with life and death situations.

I always hear their voices on the phone,
and there are customers with serious pet problems, so you should be more careful.

My rabbit had a pre-existing gastrointestinal problem, and I had been taking her to the vet for months to prevent it from worsening.

However, I feel that she didn't receive adequate treatment once she developed stasis. I lost my precious rabbit, who was only three and a half years old.

For four days after the onset of symptoms, I took her to the vet every morning without fail, and she continued to receive the same treatment of subcutaneous fluid therapy. However, her condition didn't improve, and on the fifth day, I thought that she would receive better treatment if she were hospitalized, so I requested hospitalization.

I was hoping for more aggressive treatment, such as intravenous fluid therapy. However, even after hospitalization, the treatment remained largely unchanged, and she only continued with subcutaneous fluid therapy. Blood tests and X-rays were not performed after the first day, and her condition was not re-evaluated.

As a result, after two more days, my beloved rabbit passed away.

Of course, I'm not saying she would have been saved. However, I still can't shake the feeling that there might have been room to reconsider the treatment plan, or to perform more aggressive treatments or additional tests.

The grief of losing a beloved family member is immeasurable, and even now I regret that "if we had chosen a different hospital at that time, they might have been saved."
It is a very good hospital.

Thank you so much for your help with my sugar glider's pneumonia the other day.

I would love to thank you in person, but I don't want to trouble you busy doctors, so I'm expressing my gratitude here.

Even though I rushed the visit during my work break, you still made a quick diagnosis.

Your explanations were also very thorough, and you listened patiently to my distressed state without interrupting, which was a real relief.

You explained the treatment and future treatment plan clearly, and even told me I could call to check on my sugar glider's condition while it was hospitalized. You showed such warm consideration not only for the animal but also for the person.

Thanks to you, since being discharged, my sugar glider has been taking its medication diligently, its complexion has returned to normal, it's defecating and urinating normally, and it's running around happily.

I'll never forget that terrifying moment, but now both my sugar glider and I feel so relieved.

Thank you so much!

If you are considering visiting this clinic or have felt uneasy about their response, you should carefully consider your options before seeking treatment.

I felt very uneasy about their emergency response.

Recently, I've been getting the impression that they are generally more businesslike and impersonal.

The other day, my pet's condition suddenly worsened, and when I called the veterinarian to explain the situation due to the emergency, something very unfortunate happened.

I could clearly hear the shouting of someone who seemed to be the head veterinarian from the other end of the line. Furthermore, despite my desperate attempts to explain the urgent situation, I was told the unbelievable words, "Please don't make emergency calls."

As a place where we entrust our precious lives, I feel this response in an emergency is extremely dishonest.

They should know that small animals can change suddenly, and it will be too late once something happens.

It's truly disappointing.

I had been going to this vet for five years. My ferret became ill, and I was taking him to the vet 2-4 times a week. Unfortunately, due to a misdiagnosis, my ferret passed away.

When I asked if there had been a mistake in the prescription, instead of an explanation or apology, I was pressured to sign a consent form. Furthermore, I was told they wouldn't treat my dying ferret. I felt blamed as if it were my fault, and it seemed like they were trying to cover up their own mistake. I simply cannot forgive them.

I took him to the vet because he was suffering, hoping to at least make his life easier for him while he was still alive, but the vet's actions only made things worse. I am truly heartbroken.

Also, when I asked if I could get a second opinion at another vet, the head vet said, "Do as you please, but don't come here again," and "Sign the consent form." Furthermore, for some reason, he even asked, "Are you eavesdropping?" Despite not recording anything, he said something like that, and honestly, I thought it was an unbelievable response.

I'm not asking for a refund. I simply want them to seriously consider how they treat animals, their accountability to pet owners, and their role as those responsible for caring for lives. I believe my 6-year-old ferret died due to the negligence of this hospital.

I really want the hospital director, Mr. Miwa, to be more careful. His statements, such as "Sign the consent form" and "You're eavesdropping, aren't you?", were utterly inappropriate for a veterinary hospital director, and I was even frightened.

At the time, I was in my early twenties, and I was so terrified by the director's abusive language that I couldn't do anything. Looking back now, I regret my youth and powerlessness for not speaking out properly at the time.

I still love exotic animals. However, after experiencing such terrible treatment, I no longer want to own any pets, not just exotic animals.
